Rashi on Gittin 9b:10:1.hebrew: והאיכא לשמה - דשוו גיטי נשים ושחרורי עבדים:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:10:1.english: But isn't there [the requirement of] 'for her sake' - For bills of divorce of women and bills of manumission of slaves are equal [in this requirement].

Rashi on Gittin 9b:11:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרבה - דאמר תקנתא דמוליך ומביא לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה היא, היינו מוליך ומביא:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:11:1.english: Granted, according to Rabba - who said that the enactment of "delivering and bringing" is because [the agents] are not expert in [writing] for its own sake, this is [the same as] "delivering and bringing."

Rashi on Gittin 9b:12:1.hebrew: האיכא מחובר - דפסול בתרוייהו, דכתיב (דברים כד) "וכתב ונתן" — מי שאינו מחוסר אלא כתיבה ונתינה, יצא זה שמחוסר קציצה ושחרור. גמר "לה" "לה":
Rashi on Gittin 9b:12:1.english: But there is [the case of] attached [to the ground] - For it is invalid in both [a bill of divorce and a bill of manumission], as it is written (Deuteronomy 24) "And he shall write… and give" — [this means a document] that requires nothing but writing and giving. This excludes one that also requires cutting and release [from the ground]. [For a bill of manumission,] he derives it by a verbal analogy from the word "for her" [in the verse about divorce] to "for her" [in the verse about manumission].

Rashi on Gittin 9b:12:2.hebrew: פסולא דרבנן - מוליך ומביא, רבנן הוא דאצרכוהו למימר "בפני נכתב". עד כותי, פסול מדרבנן בשאר שטרות, דאחזקינהו סתמייהו לפסולא. ערכאות, לקמיה פריך: והא ערכאות פסולא דאורייתא, שאין עדותן כשר, לפי שאינן בתורת גיטין וקידושין, ורחמנא אמר "וכתב ונתן" — מי שישנו בכלל נתינה ישנו בכלל כתיבה. והכי מפרש בפרק שני (לקמן גיטין ד' כג:):
Rashi on Gittin 9b:12:2.english: An invalidity by rabbinic law - [The case of] the one who carries and brings [the document]: it was the Rabbis who required him to say, "It was written in my presence." [The case of] a Cuthean witness: he is invalid by rabbinic law for other documents, since we presume their documents, in general, to be invalid. [The case of] gentile courts: the Gemara objects to this later: But the gentile courts are an invalidity by Torah law, for their testimony is not valid, because they are not within the framework of bills of divorce and betrothal; and the Merciful One said, "and he shall write and give" — whoever is included in the requirement of giving is included in the requirement of writing. And so it is explained in the second chapter (below, Gittin 23b).

Rashi on Gittin 9b:13:1.hebrew: בעדי מסירה - מתני' דמכשיר בשאר שטרות ופסל בהני, כגון דאיכא עדי מסירה:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:13:1.english: With witnesses of delivery - The mishna, which validates other documents but invalidates these [gentile-court documents], is [speaking] where there are witnesses of delivery.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:13:2.hebrew: ור"א היא דאמר עדי מסירה כרתי - ואין צריך לחתום בגט. וכי כתב קרא "וכתב", אכתיבת הגט כתיב, ולא אחתימת ידי עדים. ומתניתין בשכתבו סופר ישראל, ואשמעינן מתניתין דמודה ר"א במזוייף מתוכו — בחתימת עדים פסולין — שהוא פסול, ואע"ג דאיכא הכשר עדי מסירה, והאי פסולא מדרבנן, גזירה דילמא אתי למיסמך עלייהו בלא עדי מסירה. וכי אכשר ר"א היכא דלא חתימו עליה סהדי כלל:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:13:2.english: It is [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar, who said that witnesses of the transmission effect the divorce - And it is not necessary for [witnesses] to sign the bill of divorce. And when the verse writes "and he shall write," it is written about the writing of the bill, and not about the signing of the witnesses' hands. And our mishna [deals with a case] where a Jewish scribe wrote [the bill], and the mishna teaches us that Rabbi Elazar concedes in the case of a bill that is forged from within — [that is, one] signed by disqualified witnesses — that it is invalid. And even though there is the validating factor of the witnesses of the transmission, this invalidity is rabbinic, [as] a decree lest one come to rely on them [the signatures] without witnesses of the transmission. And Rabbi Elazar validates [the bill] only where witnesses did not sign on it at all.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:14:1.hebrew: אף אלו - גיטי נשים כשרים בחותמין עובדי כוכבים:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:14:1.english: Even these - Bills of divorce of women [that are signed] by gentile signatories are valid.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:14:2.hebrew: ואמר רבי זירא ירד ר"ש כו' - ואכשר להו בעדי מסירה, וכשכתבו סופר ישראל:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:14:2.english: And Rabbi Zeira said: Rabbi Shimon descended etc. - And he validated them [on the basis of] witnesses of the delivery, when a Jewish scribe wrote them.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:14:3.hebrew: מכלל דת"ק סבר לא - כרתי עדי מסירה, אלא עדי חתימה. ופסולא דאורייתא היא:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:14:3.english: By implication, the first Tanna holds not - that the witnesses of the transmission effect the divorce, but rather the witnesses of the signing. And it is a disqualification by Torah law.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:1.hebrew: העולים בערכאות של עובדי כוכבים - שנעשו השטרות על ידי בית דין של עובדי כוכבים:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:1.english: That are produced in the courts of gentiles - That the documents were executed through a court of gentiles.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:2.english: Whose signatories - The signatories that are within it.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:3.hebrew: כשרין - דדינא דמלכותא דינא, ואע"פ שהנותן והמקבל ישראלים הם:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:3.english: Valid - For the law of the kingdom is the law, even though the giver and the recipient are Jews.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:4.hebrew: חוץ מגיטי נשים - דלאו בני כריתות נינהו, הואיל ולא שייכי בתורת גיטין וקידושין. אבל על הדינין נצטוו בני נח. וכן שיחרורי עבדים, דבכל פסולא דאורייתא שוה שחרור לגט אשה, דגמרינן לה לה:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:4.english: Except for bills of divorce of women - For they (gentiles) are not subject to severance [of marriage], since they have no connection to the law of divorce and betrothal. But [gentiles] were commanded [by the Noahide laws] regarding [courts of] law. And likewise, [except for] bills of manumission of slaves, for in every disqualification [that applies] by Torah law, a bill of manumission is equal to a woman's bill of divorce, as we derive it by [the verbal analogy of] "la" "la" ("to her" "to her").

Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:6.english: To retract with regard to both of them - Before the agent has given them [to the wife or slave].

Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:7.hebrew: יחזור - דקסבר ר' מאיר: הפסד וחוב הן לאותן שנשלחו להן, ו"אין חבין לאדם אלא בפניו". כלומר, אין אדם נעשה שליח לאדם להיות נפסד על ידו, אא"כ עשאו הוא שליח, דהיינו כבפניו. ורבנן פליגי עליה דר"מ במתני', ואמרי דבשחרור אינו יכול לחזור משנמסר ליד זה, ואף ע"פ שלא עשאו העבד שליח, משום דקסברי זכות הוא לעבד שיוצא מתחת רבו לחירות, ו"זכין לו לאדם שלא בפניו", דאנן סהדי דניחא ליה דניהוי האי שלוחו להכי:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:1:7.english: He can retract - For Rabbi Meir holds that [these documents] are a loss and a liability for those to whom they were sent, and "one does not impose an obligation on a person except in his presence." That is to say, a person does not become an agent for another to cause him a loss, unless [that other person] himself appointed him as an agent, which is the equivalent of [acting] in his presence. And the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Meir in our mishna, and say that in the case of manumission he cannot retract once it has been handed to this [agent], even though the slave did not appoint him as an agent. [This is] because they hold that it is a benefit for the slave, who goes out from under his master's authority to freedom, and "one may act on behalf of a person to his benefit in his absence," for we are witnesses that he is pleased that this person be his agent for this purpose.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:2:1.english: The number - That [the Mishnah] taught "in three [ways]."

Rashi on Gittin 9b:3:1.hebrew: מקרעין להם נייר חלק - מסרטין ורושמין בסכין על הנייר את שמות העדים, ובאין העדים וממלאין את הקרעים דיו:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:3:1.english: They tear for them blank paper - They score and mark with a knife on the paper the names of the witnesses, and the witnesses come and fill the tears [i.e., the cut-out letters] with ink.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:4:1.hebrew: בגיטי נשים - משום תקנת עגונות. שמא ירצה זה המגרש לפרש בים, או מסוכן, שרוצה שלא תזקק ליבם:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:4:1.english: With regard to bills of divorce - [This is] because of the ordinance for [the sake of] *agunot*: perhaps this one who is divorcing her will want to set sail on the sea, or he is gravely ill, and he wants that she not be bound to the yavam [i.e., levirate brother].

Rashi on Gittin 9b:6:1.english: They shall not give [it] after death - And even the Rabbis, who say that the manumission of slaves is a benefit, and one may confer a benefit on a person in his absence — although [they hold that] for this purpose he has acquired it, in that [the master] cannot retract — nevertheless, the Rabbis agree that as long as the bill has not reached his [the slave's] hand, he is not freed. And since [the master] died first, the manumission is no longer a valid manumission, for the master's ownership has departed from him [the master], and the ownership of the heirs takes effect upon [the slave].

Rashi on Gittin 9b:6:2.hebrew: תנו מנה לפלוני כו' - דברי שכ"מ ככתובין וכמסורין דמו, דתקון רבנן שמא תטרף דעתו עליו בחליו אם לא היה מובטח שיקיימו דבריו:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:6:2.english: Give a maneh to so-and-so, etc. - The words of a person on his deathbed are considered as if they were written and delivered, for the Rabbis instituted this, lest his mind become troubled over it during his illness if he were not assured that his words would be fulfilled.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:7:1.english: When it teaches - Regarding those four matters.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:7:2.hebrew: מילתא דליתיה - בשאר שטרות. והא מילתא איתא בשאר שטרות: שאם מסר שטר מתנה לשלוחו ליתנו לאחר (מיתה) ומת, לא יתן לאחר מיתה, דהא לא אקני ליה ארעא עד דלימטיא שטרא לידיה, וההיא שעתא פקע ליה רשותיה:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:7:2.english: A matter that is not - found in other documents. But [this] matter does exist in other documents: for if one handed a deed of gift to his agent to give it to [the recipient] after [his] death, and [the giver] died, [the agent] may not give it after death, because [the recipient] did not acquire the land until the document reached his hand, and at that time [the giver's] ownership had already lapsed.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:9:1.hebrew: שמא לא גמר להקנותו לו - ע"פ צוואתו, בתקנה דתקון רבנן לשכיב מרע:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:9:1.english: Perhaps he did not resolve to transfer it to him - by means of his [oral] instruction, through the enactment that the Rabbis enacted for a deathly ill person.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:9:2.hebrew: אלא בשטר - לכי מטא שטרא לידיה, ליקנינהו בשטרא:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:9:2.english: Only with a deed - [He intended] that when the deed reaches his hand, he will acquire them by means of the deed.

Rashi on Gittin 9b:9:3.hebrew: ואין שטר - מקנה לאחר מיתה, דהא פקעה ליה רשותיה דנותן:
Rashi on Gittin 9b:9:3.english: And there is no deed - that conveys [ownership] after death, for the giver's ownership has already ceased.

Tosafot on Gittin 9b:12:1.hebrew: כי קתני פסולא דרבנן - אע"ג דאיכא נמי מחובר דרבנן, כגון "אין כותבין טופס שמא יכתוב תורף" (לקמן גיטין דף כא:), מ"מ עיקר מחובר דאורייתא; אבל עיקר מוליך ומביא דרבנן, אע"פ שלרבה ניתקן משום לשמה דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Gittin 9b:12:1.english: "When it teaches invalidation by rabbinic law" - Even though there is also a rabbinic [form of] "attached," such as "we do not write a template, lest he write the essential [part of the document]" (below, Gittin 21b), nevertheless the main [case of] "attached" is by Torah law. But the main [case of] "carrying and bringing" is rabbinic, even though according to Rabbah it was enacted because of "for her sake," which is by Torah law.

Tosafot on Gittin 9b:13:1.hebrew: בעדי מסירה ור"א היא - אע"ג דקתני "וכדברי ר"מ בארבעה", ה"ק: למאן דסבר כר"מ בארבעה. והא דקאמר הש"ס נמי: "אלא לר"מ מנינא למעוטי מאי?" - למאן דסבר כר"מ קאמר:
Tosafot on Gittin 9b:13:1.english: "[It is speaking] of witnesses of the transmission, and it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Elazar" - Even though [the baraita] teaches, "And like the words of Rabbi Meir in four [cases]," this is what it means to say: [it is] according to the one who holds like Rabbi Meir in four [cases]. And likewise, when the Gemara says, "But according to Rabbi Meir, what does the enumeration exclude?" - it is said with regard to the one who holds like Rabbi Meir.

Tosafot on Gittin 9b:1:1.hebrew: אע"פ שחותמיהן עובדי כוכבים כשרים חוץ מגיטי נשים - ואור"י דחותמיהן עובדי כוכבים יש לפסול אף ע"פ שכתבו ישראל, דלאו בני כריתות נינהו, כדאמרינן לקמן. ועוד, דבעינן לשמה, ועובד כוכבים אדעתא דנפשיה קא עביד, כדאמרינן בספ"ב (לקמן גיטין דף כג.). ועוד, דלאו בני שליחות נינהו, דאין שליחות לעובד כוכבים; ומדבעינן שיאמר לסופר לכתוב ולעדים חתומו, משמע דבעי שליחות. ועוד, דפסולין לעדות, ואפי' לרבי מאיר דלא הוה בעי למיפסל עבד לעדות משום דכתיב (דברים י״ט:י״ח) "שקר ענה באחיו", ועבד אחיו הוא במצות; אבל עובד כוכבים דלאו אחיו הוא, פשיטא דפסול. וכיון דלאו בני עדות נינהו, היה ראוי אפילו כל שטרות העולים בערכאות של עובדי כוכבים לפסול מן התורה, אפי' אותם העומדים לראיה; אלא תקנתא דרבנן הוא, היכא דקים לן בסהדותייהו שהוא אמת, דלא מרעי נפשייהו. ומ"מ שטר מתנה, קאמר לקמן (גיטין דף י:) דחספא בעלמא הוא, אע"ג דקים לן דקושטא קאמר, משום דהרי אין כאן שטר. ולמאי דמוקמינן לה בעדי מסירה ורבי אלעזר, היכא דכתבו ישראל לא מיפסל אלא מטעם מזוייף מתוכו:
Tosafot on Gittin 9b:1:1.english: "Even though their signatories are gentiles, they are valid, except for bills of divorce" - And the Ri says that [a bill of divorce] whose signatories are gentiles should be disqualified, even if a Jew wrote it, for they are not eligible to effect severance, as we say below. Furthermore, [a bill of divorce] must be written for its own sake, and a gentile acts with his own intention in mind, as we say at the end of the second chapter (below, Gittin 23a). Furthermore, they are not eligible to act as agents, for there is no agency for a gentile; and since [the husband] is required to say to the scribe "write" and to the witnesses "sign," this implies that agency is required. Furthermore, they are disqualified from testimony, even according to Rabbi Meir, who did not want to disqualify a slave from testimony because it is written (Deuteronomy 19:18), "He has testified falsely against his brother," and a slave is his brother with regard to the commandments; but a gentile, who is not his brother, is obviously disqualified. And since they are not eligible to give testimony, it would have been appropriate for even all documents produced in gentile courts to be disqualified by Torah law, even those that are kept as evidence; rather, it is a Rabbinic enactment, where we are confident of their testimony that it is true, because they would not harm themselves. Nevertheless, regarding a deed of gift, [the Gemara] says below (Gittin 10b) that it is a mere potsherd, even though we are confident that [the gentiles] speak the truth, because there is no [valid] document here. And according to what we establish it as [referring to] witnesses of delivery and Rabbi Elazar, where a Jew wrote it, it is disqualified only on the grounds of being "forged from within."

Tosafot on Gittin 9b:3:1.hebrew: מקרקעין להם נייר חלק - פי' בקונט': מסרטין. אע"ג דחקיקה חשיבה כתיבה, כמו כתב ע"ג טבלא ופינקס, הכא לא חשיב כתב ע"ג כתב דפסלינן בפ"ב (לקמן גיטין דף יט.), דאין כאן כתיבה גמורה אלא שרושמין קצת כדי לחתום עליו עדים. ועוד, דאפי' דיו על גבי סיקרא חשיבא לקמן בפ"ב (גז"ש) כתב לענין שבת, אע"פ שהסיקרא לבדה היא כתב. אבל לשון מקרעין לא משמע כפי' הקונט', דהוה ליה למימר מסרטין. ור"ח פי' שלוקחין נייר חלק ומקרעין עליו שמות העדים מעבר לעבר, ומשימין אותו על קלף שהגט כתוב בו, ובאין העדים וממלאים את הקרעים דיו, ונכרת הכתיבה ע"ג הגט. בירושלמי פריך: והלא כתב ראשונה הוא? פירוש: ואין הגט יכול להתקיים בחותמיו. ומשני: כשהרחיב להם את הקרעים, והעדים אין ממלאין לגמרי כל רחב הקרע:
Tosafot on Gittin 9b:3:1.english: "They tear for them blank paper" - Rashi explained in his commentary: [it means] they score [it] with lines. Even though engraving is considered writing, like [the case of] one who writes on a tablet or a notebook (pinkas), here it is not considered [as though it were] writing on top of writing, which we disqualify in the second chapter (below, Gittin 19a), because this is not complete writing; rather, they make a slight impression so that the witnesses can sign over it. Furthermore, even ink on top of red dye (sikra) is considered writing with regard to Shabbat, below in the second chapter (by verbal analogy), even though the red dye alone is [already] writing. But the term "mekarin" (tear) does not imply [what] Rashi explained in his commentary, for [if that were the meaning] it should have said "mesartin" (score). And Rabbeinu Chananel explained that they take blank paper and tear out the names of the witnesses on it, from one side [of the paper] to the other, and place it on the parchment on which the get is written, and the witnesses come and fill the tears with ink, and the writing appears on the get. In the Yerushalmi it asks: But isn't it [a case of] first writing? Meaning, the get cannot be validated through its signers. And it answers: [This is the case] where he widened the tears for them, and the witnesses do not fill in the entire width of the tear.

Tosafot on Gittin 9b:5:1.hebrew: קורין לפניהם וחותמים - ולא הוי עד מפי עד, שאין צריכין להעיד על עיקר המעשה, אלא שאומר שכך כתוב בשטר. ובעי שנים קורין, או אפילו יחיד, כגון רב נחמן וספרי דדייני דאית להו אימתא, כדלקמן בפ"ב (גיטין דף יט:):
Tosafot on Gittin 9b:5:1.english: "One reads in their presence, and they sign" - And this is not [considered] testimony from [another] witness's testimony, for [the readers] do not need to testify about the essence of the event, but only to state that this is what is written in the document. And it requires two readers, or even one, such as Rav Nachman and the scribes of the judges who inspire awe, as [stated] below in the second chapter (Gittin 19b):

Tosafot on Gittin 9b:6:1.hebrew: לא יתנו לאחר מיתה - פי' בקונטרס: ואפילו רבנן דאמרי זכות הוא לעבד, וזכין לאדם שלא בפניו — נהי דלהכי זכה דלא מצי מיהדר ביה, מודו רבנן דכל כמה דלא אתא גיטא לידיה לא הוי משוחרר. ודבר תימה פירושו: כיון דזכות הוא, פשיטא דזוכה לאלתר, כיון דאמרי' גבי שחרור "תן כזכי", כדאמר לקמן. ורש"י בעצמו חזר בו, שפי' לקמן (גיטין דף יג.) על משנה זו: דהאומר "תנו" גרסינן, ול"ג "תן" גט זה, שלא מסר ליד השליח בחייו; לפיכך לא נחלקו חכמים בדבר, לומר שמשעה ראשונה זכה לו השליח לעבד להיות משוחרר:
Tosafot on Gittin 9b:6:1.english: "They should not give [it] after death" - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that even the Rabbis, who say that it is a benefit for the slave and that we act on behalf of a person in his absence — granted that for this reason [the slave] acquires [the document], so that [the master] cannot retract — the Rabbis agree that so long as the bill has not come into the slave's hand, he is not freed. But his explanation is astonishing: since it is a benefit, it is obvious that [the slave] acquires immediately, since we say regarding manumission that "give" is like "acquire," as [the Gemara] says later. And Rashi himself retracted, for he explained later (Gittin 13a) on this mishna that we read "give" in the plural (tenu), and we do not read "give" in the singular (ten) this bill, [which indicates] that he did not hand it over to the agent during his lifetime; therefore the Sages did not dispute the matter, [so as] to say that from the first moment the agent acquired it on the slave's behalf, so that he be freed.

Tosafot on Gittin 9b:7:1.hebrew: מילתא דאיתיה בשטרות לא קתני - וא"ת: והא פסולא דערכאות בשטר מתנה, כדמפרש לקמן (גיטין דף י:), חוץ מכגיטי נשים! וי"ל: דהשתא סבר כאידך שינויא דלקמן:
Tosafot on Gittin 9b:7:1.english: "A matter that does apply to [ordinary] documents, it does not teach" - And if you ask: But the disqualification of [documents from] gentile courts applies to a deed of gift, as [the Gemara] explains below (Gittin 10b): "except for like bills of divorce of women"! And one can answer: That now [the Gemara] holds in accordance with the other answer given below:
